exposure: resolved in M01-P05 S01: an account with a registered credential no longer gets the keyring's bus in its provider's environment; the key helper asks a private broker socket of that session (a host thread that ends with the provider's process) which runs the credential command with the bus the provider never receives. A process in the provider's tree can obtain that one account's key (the provider needs it anyway) and nothing else of the keyring. Not changed: any process of the same user can still look for the abstract socket by name while the session runs, and is then served the key, because the broker checks only the user of the peer
